reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker presents OneCoin as a business opportunity, recruits partners, and directs viewers to click a link and create an account for follow-up about benefits. It promotes rising future coin values and expected capital gain, while describing paid mining-pool entry from EUR 130 and token submission to generate coins. A separate tier graphic lists euro-priced levels and token allocations, connecting the recruitment and profit claims to a concrete paid participation and token flow, although the scenarios are not guarantees and payment outcomes or projected values are not verified.

citations.quote: we are sharing and we are searching for partners who want to join us in this venture in this incredible business
All you need to do is you need to just click on the link. You can sign up completely for free just to check out the back office and how it works.
By June 2016, the expected scenario points at between 2.2 euro up to 5 euro. By June 2017, the scenario points somewhere between 50 euro and up to 100 euro.
The scenario is not a guarantee in any way
with a high demand the expected value of a single one coin will over the next couple of years increase and we can expect a very decent capital gain

opening.argument: The presentation expressly separates possible outcomes from guarantees. It labels future values as an “expected scenario,” then directly says the scenario is not guaranteed. That is a material qualification, not an assurance of profit. The discussion also presents cryptocurrency as a developing financial technology and acknowledges uncertainty by asking whether the opportunity sounds too good to be true. The evidence therefore supports conditional investment commentary with an explicit risk limitation, rather than a promise that viewers will receive returns. Even the invitation to learn more is framed as an opportunity to inspect the back office before deciding whether to participate.

citations.quote: The expected increase in value over the upcoming years is as follows
The scenario is not a guarantee in any way
Does it sound too good to be true?
You can sign up completely for free just to check out the back office and how it works.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The recruitment language shows promotion, but it does not establish deception or guaranteed returns. The prosecution's own quotations include the explicit non-guarantee. Likewise, projected values and “capital gain” are presented as expectations, not certain outcomes. The opening does not identify a promised payout, a concealed fee, or a statement that participation cannot lose money.

citations.quote: The scenario is not a guarantee in any way
You can sign up completely for free just to check out the back office and how it works.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the overall solicitation. The same presentation says the expected value will increase and that viewers can expect a “very decent capital gain.” It also directs viewers toward paid participation: joining mining pools can begin at EUR 130. Calling the projections non-guaranteed leaves the central inducement intact: pay or join now based on an emphasized prospect of appreciation and profit.

when you decide to be part of the mining pools you can start out as low as €130

opening.argument: The speaker repeatedly frames the material as an educational explanation of cryptocurrency and its underlying technology. He says the immediate purpose is to educate viewers, while the presentation explains blockchain records, distributed databases, e-wallet control, synchronization, and the absence of a single point of failure. It also offers financial education through One Academy and describes multiple education levels. That content is consistent with a technology and financial-literacy presentation that explains how a proposed system works. A later invitation to ask questions and learn more does not transform every explanatory statement into a scam claim, especially where the video does not document a completed transaction or an actual return.

citations.quote: the purpose of this video is first and foremost to educate you on what this is about
The interesting thing is that cryptocurrency is not a file on the computer.
The blockchain, or the ledger of a cryptocurrency, keeps a record of every coin, and every transaction ever made.
By joining OneCoin, you get the One Academy, a powerful financial education

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the video contains an explanation of blockchain does not prove its primary function is solicitation. The prosecution cites an invitation to partners and a signup link, but those can accompany an educational product presentation. Its opening does not show that the technical explanation is false, that money was taken from a viewer, or that any return was paid or promised as certain.

citations.quote: the purpose of this video is first and foremost to educate you on what this is about
The blockchain, or the ledger of a cryptocurrency, keeps a record of every coin, and every transaction ever made.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational framing is inseparable from the commercial pitch. The speaker says he is searching for partners, offers a free account as the entry point, and then describes paid mining pools where submitted tokens generate coins in a personal account. The technical explanation does not establish that this particular paid arrangement works, and the education label does not remove the direct recruitment and profit appeal.

citations.quote: we are sharing and we are searching for partners who want to join us in this venture
when you decide to be part of the mining pools you can start out as low as €130
by submitting your tokens will be able to generate coins to your own? Personal account

opening.argument: The observable offer can be understood as a structured business and education service: viewers receive access to One Academy, can choose among education levels, and may decide whether to enter a mining pool. The material does not show a credential request, a guaranteed return, a required downline, or a completed payment. It says a free account is available to inspect the back office before any further conversation, and the paid entry is described as starting at a stated amount rather than hidden. Whatever one thinks of the business, the supplied evidence does not establish the defining mechanism of a scam; it shows a promotional explanation of a service and participation options.

citations.quote: You can sign up completely for free just to check out the back office and how it works.
you can join the global Onecoin network you can create a free account
you can choose from six different levels of this powerful financial education
when you decide to be part of the mining pools you can start out as low as €130

rebuttal.rebuttal: The evidence supports a disclosed commercial offering, not an established scam mechanism. A paid mining-pool option is not by itself proof of fraud, and the opening does not show that payment is concealed or that a return is guaranteed. The quoted “expected” values are conditional, while the free account allows inspection before a decision. The prosecution has not supplied evidence of a completed loss, fabricated transaction, or coercive requirement.

citations.quote: You can sign up completely for free just to check out the back office and how it works.
The scenario is not a guarantee in any way

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing evidence argument overlooks what is actually described. This is not merely a retail purchase: the video ties paid mining-pool entry to token submission and coin generation in the participant's account, then links joining to a “profitable stream of income.” The absence of proof that someone was already paid does not make those inducements ordinary commerce; it means the claimed mechanism and outcome remain unverified.
